currentUserGoal: Continue the ecosystem redesign by turning the manual tile-recovery curve into real, visible Memory progression.
workCompleted: Added Fast Touch as a ten-rank permanent Memory with a 9 GT opening cost and the existing escalating touch-rank cost curve.
Placed Fast Touch on its own root-adjacent touch branch using the existing mindful-contact icon; the graph remains inside its world bounds and all connectors remain non-crossing.
Wired Fast Touch rank into live manual tile recovery, reducing the base 380 ms cooldown by 24 ms per rank to a 140 ms floor at rank ten.
Added the current recovery time to the active caretaker readout and to the redesign performance harness.
Kept old v1 permanent saves compatible by normalizing a missing fastTouchRank to zero rather than resetting progress.
Updated semantic Memory controls so Fast Touch, Broad Palm, and Many Hands are hidden during active play, disabled when locked or unaffordable, and labeled with rank and next cost.
Updated the durable ecosystem design document and expanded Memory Web and economy tests.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 119 Vitest tests across 17 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
The focused ecosystem and touch-cooldown suites passed 19 tests.
The 54-node Memory Web test confirms the Fast Touch root connection, world bounds, unique ids, and zero geometric connector crossings.
At 1280x720 on the actual redesign route, the first-run 7 GT state showed Fast Touch 0/10 at 9 GT and correctly disabled it while leaving Broad Palm affordable.
After adding prototype currency, buying Fast Touch rank 1 spent 9 GT, advanced the control to 1/10 with a 25 GT next cost, and changed the live harness cooldown from 380 ms to 356 ms.
Browser diagnostics contained no errors or warnings.

No phone viewport was rerun because the in-app browser remained fixed at 1280x720; the new node is covered by graph bounds and connector tests but still deserves the next available 390x844 visual pass.

release.status: Local ecosystem prototype checkpoint; not merged into master or promoted to production.
